task:
IndexedSet and complement sets give wrong answers in several cases. Fix all of these.

IndexedSet loses track of positions after a tail is removed out of order. Build iset = IndexedSet(range(39)), remove 0, 37, 36 and 38 in that order, then add(39). iset.index(39) must be 35, iset[-1] must be 39, and list(iset) must be list(range(1, 36)) + [39].

IndexedSet.pop accepts a float that equals the last index. IndexedSet(range(4)).pop(3.0) must raise TypeError and leave the set as [0, 1, 2, 3].

IndexedSet in-place updates with several arguments are wrong. An item must go if it is in any argument for difference_update, and if it is missing from any argument for intersection_update. IndexedSet([1, 2, 3, 4]).difference_update({1, 2}, {2, 3}) must leave [4]. IndexedSet([1, 2, 3, 4]).intersection_update({1, 2}, {2, 3}) must leave [2].

IndexedSet operations must accept one-shot iterators and lists with duplicates. For iset = IndexedSet([1, 2, 3, 4]): list(iset.intersection(iter([2, 3, 5]))) must be [2, 3], list(iset.difference(iter([2, 3, 5]))) must be [1, 4], and list(iset.symmetric_difference(iter([2, 3, 5]))) must be [1, 4, 5]. A repeated value in the operand counts once: iset = IndexedSet([1, 2]); iset ^= [2, 2, 5, 5] must leave [1, 5].

The sets returned by complement() break set algebra. Read complement(s) as everything except s, and complement(complement(s)) as s. For any sets a and b, including the empty set and a full universe such as range(6), the operators &, &=, ^, ^=, |, |=, - and -= must give the same membership as plain set math. This must hold on every value in the universe, for every pairing of operand forms: complement(complement(s)) with complement(s) in both orders, each form with itself, and each form with a plain set on either side. So the left operand may be a plain set, and an in-place operator must leave the correct result. Examples: complement(complement({1, 2})) & complement({1}) must contain 2 and not 1. After x = complement({1}); x &= {1, 2}, x must contain 2 and must not contain 1 or 3. complement({1, 2}) ^ {2, 3} and the ^= form must contain 2 and 4 and must not contain 1 or 3.

Everything else must keep working.
accept: PYTHONPATH=.bench-deps python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider tests
